messages:
elaine: flagging a proposal — we should treat short-lived request logs (trace + headers) as 'ephemeral' by default and apply automatic de-identification before they hit long-term storage. want opinions on policy + console UX for opt-outs.

raj: agree in principle. curious about what we mean by de-identification — full redaction vs pseudonymization?

elaine: prefer layered approach: 1) automatic pattern-based scrub (emails, SSNs, credit cards) 2) route-level tokenization for user identifiers (pseudonymize) 3) opt-in to full-raw retention for debug routes with audit logs.

kevin: sounds reasonable. need to spell out retention windows and who can request raw. ops + security will need an approval workflow. also: perf cost for on-the-fly tokenization?

sophia: tokenization should be cheap — we can reuse existing hashing keys (KMS) and rotate. main cost is extra bytes in telemetry pipeline + a slight CPU hit at ingest. quantify it.

jamie: UX question: in Console, do we expose per-route toggles (ephemeral on/off, raw retention TTL) or only org-level defaults with request for exceptions?

elaine: thinking defaults at org-level + per-route overrides. per-route overrides require a justification field + an audit entry. non-admins can request via audit workflow.

matt: from routing perspective, traffic that goes to dedicated/private should mirror the same policy unless customer opts out for private infra. make sure the policy is enforceable client-side (sdk header) and server-side validated.

raj: edge case: function/tool-calls that include API keys in payloads — our scrub rules need to catch key-like strings. propose adding entropy heuristics + pattern rules.

kevin: +1. also need a rule for embeddings outputs — we should never store raw user-provided text for embedding endpoints unless explicitly retained. default should be ephemeral and hashed.

ops-bot: note: current pipeline supports regex redaction and sha256 hashing via `redwood-telemetry` v2.1. deploying new rules requires migration run `telemetry/migrate-deid-v2`.

elaine: quick config sketch for Console and backend (proposal):

```
# per-org defaults
telemetry.deid.default: true
telemetry.deid.retain_raw_ttl_days: 7
telemetry.deid.deid_level: pattern+hash
telemetry.deid.per_route_overrides_enabled: true

# override requires: {requester, justification, expire_ts}
```

sophia: looks good. add `telemetry.deid.allow_debug_raw = ["route-a","route-b"]` with a forced audit webhook to security.

jamie: for Console UX: expose a single control with three states: Strict (patterns only, 7d), Pseudonymize (hash ids, 14d), Raw-with-approval (30d, requires audit). clicking Raw opens a modal to request approval. show active audit entries in the route sidebar.

matt: rollout plan: start with opt-in for internal teams, collect cost delta and missed-debug incidents for 4 weeks, then flip org default to strict-ephemeral after bugs. mirror setting in Dedicated control plane for enterprise customers.

raj: sampling: by default we should sample 1% of requests for full raw retention for debugging across routes, but exclude sensitive routes. allow increasing sample rate per-route for canaries.

kevin: implement sampling with stable hashing of request ids so samples are reproducible per user & per route. avoid correlated sampling across services.

elaine: open questions: 1) retention TTLs (7 vs 14 days), 2) what qualifies as "sensitive route" (PII-sensitive vs regulatory), 3) console visibility for auditors.

sophia: for (3) auditors need read-only view + ability to trigger emergency raw-unmasking with break-glass; that action must create immediate audit log + pager.

jamie: UI mockups incoming — i'll drop a Figma link shortly.

matt: will add telemetry cost estimate task to infra backlog (TKT-4212).

elaine: thanks. action items: jamie -> mockups + modal text; kevin -> secure hashing + perf estimate; raj -> list of sensitive routes + heuristic rules; sophia -> KMS rotation implications; matt -> sampling implementation doc. we'll reconvene Fri. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled rollout window created for `telemetry-deid-v2` on 2026-03-21 02:00 UTC.
